name: Bachelor of Arts
description:
Avondale's Bachelor of Arts covers more scientific ground than the name implies. Biological Science, Chemistry and Mathematics all sit as available majors alongside the humanities staples (English, History, Music, Communication, Religious Studies), a structural quirk that comes from Avondale folding its science majors into the BA rather than running them exclusively through the Bachelor of Science. Students pick an 8-unit major and can add a 4-unit minor from the same list, or take strands borrowed from Business or Ministry and Theology to build a more interdisciplinary profile.

The Communication major is the one with a defined career on-ramp built into the structure: it requires a professional internship in the final year, placing students with media, marketing, or communications employers rather than leaving that experience to chance. Chaplaincy is the other major with embedded work-integrated learning, reflecting Avondale's role training pastoral and chaplaincy staff for Adventist schools and hospitals across the region.
curriculum:
24 units, 144 credit points, three years full-time
Major (8 units) chosen from: Biological Science, Chaplaincy, Chemistry, Communication, English, Food & Nutrition, History, Mathematics, Music, Religious Studies, Visual Arts
Optional minor (4 units) from the same list, or a strand from Business or Ministry & Theology
Christian Studies core units
Communication major: Professional Internship unit in final year
Chaplaincy major: work-integrated learning embedded across CHPL-coded units
General elective units to complete the 24-unit total

name: Bachelor of Arts/Bachelor of Teaching (Secondary)
description:
This is Avondale's combined arts/teaching degree for people who know from day one they want to teach secondary school. It runs longer than the standalone BA (the paired BSc/BTeaching runs 32 units over four years, and this Arts equivalent follows a similar extended structure) because it has to satisfy both a full arts major and NSW Education Standards Authority accreditation requirements for secondary teaching in that subject area.

Graduates come out with two teaching methods areas typically drawn from English, History, Music, or Religious Studies, which matters practically: secondary schools, and especially the Adventist school system Avondale feeds heavily into, hire teachers who can cover two subjects on a timetable, not one. Professional experience placements are substantial and staged across the degree, from early observation placements in first year building up to a full practicum block in final year, rather than concentrated into a single end-of-course prac.
curriculum:
Combined BA content major (8 units) plus a second teaching method area, drawn from English, History, Music, or Religious Studies
Education core: Educational Psychology, Curriculum and Pedagogy, Classroom Management, Assessment and Reporting
Professional experience placements staged from Year 1 observation through to a capstone full-time practicum block in final year
NSW Education Standards Authority (NESA)-accredited secondary teaching methods units
Christian Studies core units
Final-year Professional Studies seminar preparing for graduate teacher accreditation
english_requirements: IELTS 7.5 (no band below 7.0) or equivalent (teaching registration requirement)

name: Bachelor of Business
description:
The Bachelor of Business at Avondale is a 24-unit degree structured around double majors rather than a single specialisation. Most students pair accounting with a second area (marketing, HR, or business administration) or take a major-and-minor combination, and the accounting major itself carries accreditation from both CPA Australia and Chartered Accountants ANZ, which matters if the end goal is a CA or CPA designation later.

The smaller cohort size compared to a metropolitan business school shows up in practice: internship placements are built into the course rather than bolted on as an optional extra, and Avondale's business faculty draws on its Sydney campus location (Wahroonga) for placements with businesses and Adventist-affiliated organisations across Sydney's north. Christian Studies core units run alongside the standard business core, including accounting, economics, management, marketing, and law, reflecting the university's integration of faith and vocation rather than treating them as separate tracks.
curriculum:
Business core (Years 1–2): Financial Accounting, Economics, Marketing Principles, Business Law, Management, Business Statistics, Business Communication
Major 1 and Major 2 (or major + minor), selected from Accounting, Marketing, Human Resource Management, Business Administration, with an Entrepreneurship minor available
Christian Studies core units (compulsory across all Avondale undergraduate degrees)
Professional internship unit, undertaken within a major or minor field of study
Capstone: Strategic Management or equivalent integrative unit in final semester
Elective units to complete 144 credit points across 24 units

name: Bachelor of Nursing
description:
Nursing is arguably the program Avondale is best known for outside its own denomination, largely because of the pipeline into Sydney Adventist Hospital ('the San') and other major health networks across the Hunter and Central Coast region. The course runs 24 units over six full-time semesters and builds in more clinical hours than the accreditation minimum: students log at least 800 hours of professional experience placement, starting from semester two once first-year prerequisites and pre-clinical checks (police check, vaccination status, National Police Certificate) are cleared.

What distinguishes the Avondale version from a standard metropolitan nursing degree is the deliberate inclusion of a whole-person model of care, a legacy of the university's Seventh-day Adventist health philosophy, which has produced a genuine research output in lifestyle medicine and preventive health (the same tradition behind the Blue Zones research on Adventist longevity in Loma Linda, California, that Avondale's own academics have contributed to). Clinical rotations cover acute medical/surgical wards, emergency and ICU exposure, maternal and child health, mental health, aged care and community settings, so graduates aren't narrowly trained into one specialty before they've even sat the registration exam.
curriculum:
Year 1: Foundations of Nursing Practice, Anatomy & Physiology I & II, Introduction to Professional Nursing, Psychology for Health Professionals
Year 1 Semester 2: first clinical placement block begins (subject to pre-clinical clearance)
Year 2: Medical-Surgical Nursing, Mental Health Nursing, Pathophysiology & Pharmacology, Research in Nursing Practice, extended clinical placements in acute and high-dependency settings
Year 3: Maternal & Child Health Nursing, Aged Care and Chronic Disease Management, Community and Primary Health Care Nursing, Emergency and Critical Care Nursing, capstone Transition to Professional Practice placement
Minimum 800 hours supervised clinical placement across acute, community, mental health and aged care settings
Registration pathway: eligible for AHPRA registration as a Registered Nurse on graduation

name: Bachelor of Science
description:
The standalone Bachelor of Science at Avondale is smaller than its BA counterpart in terms of enrolments, since several of the science disciplines (Biological Science, Chemistry, Food & Nutrition, Mathematics) are also offered as majors within the Bachelor of Arts. Students choosing the BS specifically want the science degree title, often because it reads better for graduate entry into health science postgraduate courses, dietetics, or laboratory-based careers.

Food & Nutrition is worth flagging as a genuine point of difference: it draws on Avondale's Adventist health heritage (the same institutional lineage that produced Sanitarium and its Weet-Bix brand a century ago) and is taught with a research base in lifestyle and preventive health rather than as a generic nutrition science unit bolted onto a chemistry-heavy degree. Students combining it with Biological Science are well placed for further study in dietetics or public health.
curriculum:
Major (8 units) chosen from Biological Science, Chemistry, Food & Nutrition, or Mathematics
Core mathematics and science foundation units in Year 1
Second major or 4-unit minor from the same disciplines
Laboratory-based practical units across chemistry and biological science majors
Christian Studies core units
Research or research-methods unit in final year for students proceeding to honours or postgraduate study
24 units, 144 credit points, three years full-time

name: Bachelor of Theology
description:
Avondale runs one of the only standalone Bachelor of Theology degrees in Australia housed within a Seventh-day Adventist institution, and the course reflects that heritage directly: alongside standard biblical studies and biblical languages (Greek and Hebrew feature prominently), students work through Adventist doctrinal history and the denomination's distinctive eschatology, taught by faculty attached to the Seminary at the Cooranbong campus.

Most students aren't just doing this for personal interest. A large share go on to ministerial credentialing within the Adventist Church across Australia and the Pacific, or use the degree as the entry point into postgraduate theological study (Avondale's own Master of Arts in Theology, or seminaries overseas). The course is unapologetically confessional rather than comparative-religion in orientation, which is worth knowing going in: this isn't a general religious studies degree, it's training within a specific tradition.
curriculum:
24 units, 144 credit points, six full-time semesters
Biblical Studies core: Old Testament Introduction, New Testament Introduction, Biblical Hermeneutics
Biblical languages: Greek I & II, Hebrew I & II
Systematic and Adventist Theology units, including denominational history and eschatology
Christian History and Church History units
Practical/Pastoral units: homiletics (preaching), pastoral care, mission and evangelism
Elective units and a research or ministry-placement capstone in final year

name: Master of Arts
description:
Avondale's Master of Arts is a coursework postgraduate degree that mirrors the BA's breadth into postgraduate territory, with a Theology and Religious Studies concentration being the most established pathway given the Seminary's presence on the Cooranbong campus. Students who did their undergraduate degree elsewhere and want to formalise theological study without committing to a full Master of Divinity often land here.

Because cohorts are small, the degree runs with a good deal of supervisory attention per student, and a research project or minor thesis component in the final stage of the degree is standard rather than optional. This isn't a pure coursework-only credential; it expects candidates to produce a piece of independent research under supervision by the end.
curriculum:
Coursework units in the chosen discipline (e.g. Theology, Religious Studies, English, History)
Research Methods unit (compulsory)
Advanced seminar units in the specialisation area
Minor thesis or research project, undertaken in the final stage under individual supervision
Elective units to complete the total credit point requirement for the degree

name: Master of Education
description:
Avondale's Master of Education is built for working teachers rather than career-changers. Every unit runs by distance, with a single Winter School each July drawing students back to the Lake Macquarie campus for a week of face-to-face intensives. That residential week matters more than it sounds: it's where the small cohort (Avondale's education postgrad numbers stay modest compared to the Group of Eight providers) actually meets in person, and where the program's Christian education strand gets taught alongside the research methodology core.

The degree suits teachers chasing a leadership track, a curriculum specialisation, or simply the credential bump for promotion within Adventist and independent school systems, where an Avondale postgrad carries particular weight. Because it's capped at eight units (48 credit points) and deliberately excludes a full-time pathway (Avondale is upfront that some units simply aren't offered often enough to support one), most candidates are two to three years into full-time teaching before they enrol, doing the degree one or two units a semester around a teaching load.
curriculum:
EDUC50000 Introduction to Educational Research (compulsory)
One compulsory unit in Christian Education (theological/philosophical foundations)
Specialisation stream: 4 units drawn from a single list (e.g. leadership, curriculum, literacy, or special/inclusive education) for a named specialisation, or
General stream: 4 elective units drawn across multiple specialisation lists for an unspecialised MEd
2 remaining units to complete the 8-unit, 48 credit-point total
Winter School residential (July, Lake Macquarie campus) attached to select units
No capstone thesis in the standard coursework pattern; research-intensive exit available via an extended project unit in some strands
admission_requirements: An Australian four-year Bachelor's degree in Education, a Bachelor's degree followed by a Diploma of Education, a Bachelor of Teaching, an Australian Graduate Certificate in Educational Studies, an Australian Master of Teaching, or an equivalent overseas qualification; applicants must also submit a resume/written summary showing at least two years of relevant work experience.
english_requirements: IELTS overall 7.5 with no sub-band below 7.0 (or a recognised alternative under Avondale's Admission Policy, e.g. a prior qualification taught and assessed in English within the last two years in an approved English-speaking country).

name: Master of Leadership and Management
description:
A 12-unit postgraduate degree aimed at people already in, or heading into, management roles who want the credential without leaving their job. It's delivered by distance with a mid-year residential intensive, which is the only time the cohort is physically together. One compulsory unit, LAMC50600 Theology, Theory and Practice of Leadership, signals the degree's actual orientation: it treats leadership as something with an ethical and, specifically, a Christian dimension, not just a set of management techniques lifted from a generic MBA-style curriculum.

Compared to Avondale's separate Master of Business Administration, this degree sits closer to organisational leadership than finance or strategy: it's a reasonable fit for people running teams in healthcare, education, ministry, or not-for-profit settings where Avondale's networks (particularly Adventist Church institutions across the Pacific) provide a natural graduate destination, though it isn't restricted to those sectors.
curriculum:
LAMC50600 Theology, Theory & Practice of Leadership (compulsory)
Core units in Organisational Behaviour, Strategic Management, and Human Resource Leadership
Research methods unit
Elective units selected from leadership specialisations (change management, conflict resolution, or health/education-sector leadership streams)
Mid-year residential intensive (on-campus attendance required for designated units)
12 units total, offered in two study patterns over a maximum candidature of 5 years

name: Master of Nursing (Coursework)
description:
This is Avondale's postgraduate nursing pathway for registered nurses who already hold a first degree and want to specialise rather than start over. At 11 units (72 credit points) it's a lean coursework masters, and it's built with defined exit points: a Graduate Certificate at 4 units, a Graduate Diploma at 8, so a nurse who needs to pause partway through still walks away with a recognised credential rather than nothing.

The two specialisation tracks on offer, Clinical Nursing/Clinical Teaching and Leadership and Management, split off after five shared core units, and the choice matters for career direction: one leads toward advanced clinical practice or clinical education roles (increasingly in demand as hospital-based clinical facilitator positions expand), the other toward nurse unit manager and health service leadership positions. Given Avondale's ties to Sydney Adventist Hospital, a number of students are already working within that network while completing the degree part-time.
curriculum:
Core units (5): Advanced Nursing Practice, Research Methods in Health, Health Policy and Systems, Evidence-Based Practice, Professional and Ethical Issues in Nursing
Specialisation A — Clinical Nursing/Clinical Teaching: 6 specialty units in advanced clinical assessment, clinical education and supervision, and specialty clinical practice
Specialisation B — Leadership and Management: 6 specialty units in health service management, leadership theory and practice, and organisational change in health settings
Exit points: Graduate Certificate in Nursing (4 units/24 CP), Graduate Diploma in Nursing (8 units/48 CP)
Full Master of Nursing: 11 units/72 credit points
admission_requirements: Bachelor degree in nursing or related discipline
